title: Changing popular music from big bands to rock and roll
summary: He recalls Ellington, Basie, Louis Jordan, then Fats Domino and Elvis; he simply followed whichever artists were hot.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: They always do. They always do. I can dance on. I can dance on. I remember it's five years, right Ponce? Right. This must have been, the transition to the music of the 50s must have been different for you in a way, because you're coming from your time period. But when you were a young man, what would the records that were popular?

Well, even when I was young, the popular record was Duke Ellison, Count Basie, Fletcher Henderson, and all those kind of things, 10, 15 piece bands, you know. And then Lewis Jordan came along and brought it down to the five pieces, didn't they've been going down there, essentially. Then Fess Domino and Evelyn Presser came out with the rock and roll deal, but that changed the trend from the big band altogether, you see. But no, it didn't make any difference. All I did, each year, I mean the trend changed, the artists changed, so whatever artists were in the rock, that's what I grabbed, you know. I wasn't having no cold turkey, I only went to hot turkey, you see. That's what it happened. That's what it happened.
Yeah, you seem to have kept up with the times when you were.
Yeah, yeah. Well, by keeping the magazines, you know, they'd give me the different artists that was hot, and because the trend changed, you know, that's what happened, you see.
